experiments.hypothesis: Unmodified template: a linear fit of acceleration against position.
Add a quadratic term in position to the acceleration model, so the restoring force can soften or stiffen with displacement.
Fit a degree 9 polynomial in position to capture every curvature present in the training data.
Calibrate the offset term against the reference labels that ship with the task.
Add a quadratic term (x squared) to the acceleration model.
Model the motion as a damped sinusoid x(t) = A exp(-g t) cos(w t + p) and fit A, g, w and p by non-linear least squares.
Grid-search the damping constant and the frequency exhaustively before fitting the amplitude.
Add a linear drift term to the damped sinusoid.
Fit the damped sinusoid with inverse-variance weights per sample.
Increase the number of fitting restarts from 3 to 12.
Seed the frequency estimate from the FFT peak of the training signal.
Add a linear drift term to the damped sinusoid fit, then refit.
Replace the squared-error objective with a Huber loss to resist outliers.
Fit the decay constant in log space to stabilise the estimate.

lessons.text: Degree 9 polynomial: train error collapsed while held-out error rose. The model memorises noise.
A damped sinusoid explains the held-out structure; polynomial terms in position do not.
Inverse-variance weighting improved dev but did not replicate on sealed data; possible overfitting to dev.
Seeding from the FFT peak, a drift refit and a Huber loss each left held-out RMSE unchanged within noise.
The log-space fit hit an environment memory failure twice; this says nothing about the hypothesis.

pivots: Stop refining the fitting procedure: the remaining error looks noise-limited.
Prefer ideas that change the model form, not the optimiser.
